title: Create slim projection tables + index maintenance automation for control-plane
creator: Ava Martinez
description: This ticket implements a two-part plan to reduce control-plane query amplification and maintenance overhead by (1) pulling frequently queried fields out of wide JSONB blobs into normalized slim projection tables and (2) introducing an automated index maintenance and reindexing pipeline with partition-aware heuristics and adaptive autovacuum settings.
background: We continue to see a pattern where one-off JSONB payloads are read by hot queries leading to large heap + index scans and expensive VACUUM/REINDEX windows. Previous work (see ENG-46805 and ENG-75213) moved some columns out of JSONB, but hot reads and index bloat remain for the tenant/ownership/query hot paths. Operationally, reindex jobs are manual and heavy; autovacuum is too generic for mixed hot/cold partitions.
goals: 1) Reduce average control-plane tail latency for tenant list and project lookup queries by 40% under 95th percentile loads. 2) Reduce index bloat > 10% by automated reindex schedule and targeted partial indexes. 3) Provide safe online schema change pattern and rollback. 4) Reduce peak reindex maintenance windows and eliminate manual interventions.
out_of_scope: Application-level model changes outside control-plane (e.g., runtime inference APIs), full JSONB denormalization of rarely-read audit payloads.
scope:
- Introduce slim_projection_{entity} tables for tenant, project, user_ownership with stable surrogate PKs and minimal columns used by hot queries.
- Backfill data via streaming background worker that reads JSONB and writes to projection tables with idempotency keys.
- Replace hot read paths to select from projections and join to audit blob only when needed.
- Implement index_maintenance service that: schedules per-partition reindexing based on bloat heuristics, triggers online reindex for small partitions, and emits signals for manual review for large partitions.
- Apply adaptive autovacuum settings per partition tier (hot/warm/cold) via pg_class augmentation and helper functions.
- Add dashboards and alerts for bloat growth, reindex backlog, and projection sync lag.
migration_plan:
Phase 1: create projection tables (no writes), add background backfill worker with high parallelism throttled by CPU.
Phase 2: shadow reads — ensure projection reads return identical results to JSONB queries for a sampling window; add QA compare job.
Phase 3: flip read path to projection tables for selected services with canary (10% -> 50% -> 100%).
Phase 4: mark JSONB columns as deprecated, schedule periodic compaction/archival to audit_shadow table.
Phase 5: run index_maintenance full rollout and tune autovacuum.
Each phase includes rollback: revert application read switch, stop worker, and drop newly created cron jobs. Backfill is idempotent; operations can be paused and resumed.
backfill_strategy: Use a dedicated backfill worker fleet (k8s job) that streams primary keys from the source table in ranges and performs UPSERT into projection tables in idempotent batches. Job tracks progress via backfill_checkpoint table. Use rate limiting: max 2000 rows/sec per worker with exponential backoff on DB errors. Backfill preserved ordering per-tenant to reduce contention.
index_maintenance_design: A new service 'index_maintainer' runs on a weekly cadence and performs: 1) compute bloat metrics per-index using pg_stat and pgstattuple heuristics, 2) mark indexes for online reindex if bloat > 35% and index size < 10GB, otherwise mark for manual review and snapshot. 3) schedule reindexing tasks during off-peak windows with tenant-aware throttles. 4) update per-partition autovacuum settings using ALTER TABLE SET (autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor = X, autovacuum_vacuum_threshold = Y) where X/Y are chosen based on write-rate percentiles.
observability: Dashboards: controlplane.index_bloat (time-series by index), controlplane.projection_sync_lag (per entity, percentiles), controlplane.reindex_queue (pending/running), controlplane.autovacuum_events (count & duration). Alerts: >50% of hot partitions tagged 'needs-reindex' for 72h OR projection_sync_lag P95 > 2m for 1h.
testing_plan: Unit tests for backfill idempotency, integration tests for shadow read parity (compare results over 1k random keys), load test that simulates 10k QPS for read path and verifies 95th latency improvement after flip. Run reindex in staging with representative partitions and validate zero-downtime behavior. Use canary on staging cluster with traffic shaping.
rollback_plan:
- Stop index_maintainer and backfill workers.
- Revert application read path to JSONB sources via feature flag.
- Restore previous autovacuum settings from snapshot table.
- If schema changes were applied (concurrent indexes), drop new indexes created during rollout (concurrently).
risk_and_mitigation:
Risk: backfill introduces write amplification causing replication lag. Mitigation: throttle backfill concurrency and set write budget per region.
Risk: reindex for large index may cause temporary IO pressure. Mitigation: enforce size threshold and require manual approval for >10GB indexes; use pg_repack for minimal locking if needed.
Risk: logical divergence between projection and source while running. Mitigation: add a QC compare job and stop flip if divergence > 0.1% for >1h.
post_rollout_tasks:
- Remove deprecated JSONB columns after 90 days.
- Add schema comments and data dictionary entries in Confluence.
- Schedule quarterly index maintenance audit.
- Codify autovacuum tunables in infra repo for reproducibility.
observed_metrics_baseline: Current: projects.owner query P95 = 240ms, 95th tokenized controlplane tail contributes ~30% of latency; index bloat median = 28%, top 10 indexes mean size = 6.8GB.
expected_outcomes: P95 reductions on hot queries by ~40%, projected disk savings of 15-25% for hot partitions, reduced manual DBA interventions by 80% within 3 months.
notes: This ticket is intentionally conservative: we avoid wholesale JSONB denormalization up-front and focus on the smallest set of columns that materially affect hot reads. If Phase 1 demonstrates >60% latency gain, we will accelerate follow-ups and re-evaluate partitioning schema for extremely hot tenants.
